claim: The paper presents a quantitative theory describing the mixing of two identical powders in a horizontal barrel mixer.
quote: describes the mixing of two identical powders in a horizontal barrel mixer

claim: When two components are loaded end-to-end in a simple barrel mixer, mixing can occur only by diffusion.
quote: loaded end-to-end in a simple barrel mixer, mixing can occur only by diffusion

claim: The degree of mixedness is a fundamental state of a system, completely independent of the means by which it is achieved.
quote: The degree of mixedness is a fundamental state of a system

claim: Two independent fundamental mechanisms are required for mixing: macro-mixing (bringing components together) and micromixing (particle diffusion across boundaries).
quote: brought together, and (2) individual particles must diffuse across boundaries

claim: Mechanical macro-mixing alone cannot produce a high degree of mixedness in finite time unless micromixing takes place simultaneously.
quote: unless micromixing can take place simultaneously

claim: Prior mixing experiments either could not test mixing theories or could not be accounted for by a general theory, motivating experiments on an ideal system.
quote: experiments could not be designed to check the validity of theories of mixing

claim: The mixing process is considered analogous to diffusion in gases, liquids, or solids, so Fick's second law applies.
quote: the process can be considered as analogous to diffusion in gases

claim: In a horizontal barrel mixer rotating about its axis, particle motion along the axis results only from random inter-particle collisions.
quote: result from inter-particle collisions and will therefore be completely random

claim: For an ideal system of identical diffusing components, the diffusion coefficient can be assumed independent of concentration.
quote: the diffusion coefficient can be assumed to be independent of concentration

claim: The derived concentration solution (Eq. 4) is similar in form to Lacey's more general equation and equivalent to it under the present conditions.
quote: Equation (4) is similar in form to the more general equation given by LACEY [5]

claim: The degree of mixedness M is defined after Lacey from the unmixed, random, and true variances, going from 0 to 1.
quote: Lacey defined the degree of mixedness M, at any number of revolutions, N, as

claim: Lacey's mixedness parameter was modified because the original M can exceed unity when the true variance falls below the random variance.
quote: it is possible to obtain values of M greater than unity

claim: For long mixing times M(N) fluctuates about a random degree of mixedness M_r below unity, which depends only on sample size and tends to unity as sample size increases.
quote: function of the sample size only and tends to unity as the sample size increases

claim: For large numbers of revolutions, a plot of log sigma(N) vs N yields a straight line of slope -pi^2 D / (2.303 L^2).
quote: plot of $\log \sigma(N)$ vs N should yield a straight line

claim: During the early stage of mixing, a plot of sigma^2(N) vs sqrt(N) gives a straight line of slope -(4/L) sqrt(2D/pi).
quote: plot of $\sigma^{2}(N)$ vs $\sqrt{N}$ should give a straight line

claim: The need for two kinetic equations does not imply a change in mixing kinetics; both are approximations to the same general equation valid over the whole range of N.
quote: does not imply a change in the kinetics at any stage in the process

claim: Essentially identical components were required for the ideal system so that differences in density, particle shape, or surface roughness would not influence the mixing kinetics.
quote: effects due to differences in density, particle shape, or surface roughness

claim: The mixer was a 4-in. diameter lucite tube, 16 in. long, fitted with 8-in. diameter lucite end flanges.
quote: a 4-in. dia. lucite tube, 16 in. long

claim: The two lots of glass beads were identical in all respects except color (white and yellow) and refractive index (1.91 and 1.88, respectively).
quote: identical in all respects except for differences in color (white and yellow)

claim: The mixer was loaded to 60 per cent of its total volume (beads plus voids), composed of equal weights of the white and yellow beads.
quote: A load of 60 per cent (beads plus voids) of the total volume was used

claim: The mixer speed was at all times 27 rev/min, approximately 20 per cent of the critical speed.
quote: The mixer speed was at all times 27 rev/min

claim: For sampling purposes, the mixer was divided into fifteen sections one inch apart and at right angles to the mixer axis.
quote: the mixer was divided into fifteen sections one inch apart

claim: Of the thirteen sampling positions assigned to each section, two were chosen at random and their mean represented the section concentration.
quote: Of the thirteen possible locations on each section, two were chosen at random

claim: Sampling used a vacuum chamber connected to a hypodermic needle raised and lowered through the template, allowing accurate concentration determination with minimal disturbance of the charge.
quote: a vacuum chamber connected to a hypodermic needle

claim: Samples were assayed by visual counting with a petrographic microscope; white and yellow beads were distinguished because their refractive indices bracket that of the immersion liquid.
quote: As the refractive index of the white beads was greater than that of the liquid

claim: For a sample size of 500 particles, the sensitivity of the sampling method is plus-or-minus 0.2 per cent (one particle).
quote: For a sample size of 500 particles, the sensitivity is ±0·2 per cent

claim: Because sampling is direct visual counting of particles of each type, the accuracy is within plus-or-minus 1 per cent and the precision is quite high.
quote: the accuracy is within ±1 per cent and the precision is quite high

claim: There is no systematic variation in concentration perpendicular to the mixer axis, confirming that the system mixes via uniform diffusion across the original interface.
quote: no systematic variation in concentration perpendicular to the mixer axis

claim: The diffusion coefficient values evaluated by four different methods agree very closely.
quote: are compared in Table 3. The values agree very closely

claim: Experimental concentration data agree excellently with theoretical curves calculated using the average diffusion coefficient.
quote: the agreement between theory and experiment is excellent

claim: Mixing occurs in two kinetic stages: early on the degree of mixedness is proportional to the square root of the number of revolutions, later log(1-M) is linear in revolutions; the kinetics data agree very well with these predictions.
quote: proportional to the square root of the time of mixing (number of revolutions)

claim: The previously implied reflection of the diffusion front at the mixer end has no theoretical or physical justification, since it would require diffusion against a concentration gradient.
quote: this concept has no theoretical or physical justification

claim: With fifteen samples the predicted unmixed sample variance is 0.25, but if the sampling probe missed the original interface it would be 0.267, explaining positive deviations at low numbers of revolutions.
quote: the unmixed sample variance would then be 0·267

claim: In the later stages of the process, the degree of mixedness as a function of the number of revolutions is described by an exponential relationship.
